{{Short description|Field extension of rational numbers}}
{{Use American English|date = January 2019}}
An '''elementary number''' is one formalization of the concept of a [[closed-form number]]. Roughly speaking, it is a complex number that can be specified using algebraic operations, [[exponentiation]], and [[logarithm]]s.

Several different kinds of elementary numbers appear in the literature.

An elementary number of [[Joseph Fels Ritt]] is built from an integer by applying finitely many <math>\Q</math>-algebraic operations (i.e. <math>\Q</math>-algebraic functions), exponential functions, and/or logarithm functions.<ref>{{cite book|last=Ritt|first=Joseph Fels|title=Integration in finite terms. Liouville's theory of elementary methods|location=New York|publisher=Columbia University press|year=1948|page=60}}</ref> The set of these numbers is the smallest subfield of <math>\C</math> that is algebraically closed and closed under <math>\exp</math> and <math>\ln</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Lin|first=Ferng-Ching|title=Schanuel's conjecture implies Ritt's conjectures|journal=Chin. J. Math.|volume=11|number=1|year=1983|pages=41–50}}</ref> An elementary number is a constant <math>\Q</math>-elementary function.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Umemura|first=Hiroshi|title=On a class of numbers generated by differencial equations related with <math>\Q</math>-algebraic groups|journal=Nagoya Math. J.|volume=133|year=1994|pages=1–55|doi=10.1017/S0027763000004736|doi-access=free}}</ref>

An exponential-logarithmic number of Timothy Y. Chow is built from an integer by applying finitely many field operations (i.e. rational functions) over <math>\Q</math>, exponential functions, and/or logarithm functions. The set of these numbers is the intersection of all subfields of <math>\C</math> that are closed under exp and ln. It is closed under the field operations, <math>\exp</math> and <math>\ln</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chow|first=Timothy|title=What is a closed-form number|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|volume=106|number=5|year=1999|pages=440–448|doi=10.1080/00029890.1999.12005066|s2cid=3256250}}</ref>

An elementary number of Daniel Richardson is a solution of a special kind of system of exponential polynomial equations.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Richardson|first=Daniel|title=How to recognize zero|journal=Journal of Symbolic Computation|volume=24|number=6|year=1997|pages=627–645|doi=10.1006/jsco.1997.0157|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Chow's numbers can be presented explicitly, i.e. by applying rational, exponential and logarithmic functions, whereas Ritt's and Richardson's sets also allow implicit presentation, i.e. solutions of <math>\Q</math>-algebraic equations respectively special exponential-logarithmic polynomial systems.
